1 
 
 
Conway Ice Rink Commission Meeting  
July 14, 2026 
10:30 AM 
Conway Arena Conference Room 
5 Stadium Drive 
Nashua, NH 03062 
 
 
Call to Order 
The 2026 annual meeting was called to order at 10:36 AM by Charlie Hall. 
 
Members in Attendance 
Lori Wilshire 
Megan Caron 
Charlie Hall 
Lauren Byers 
 
Also in Attendance 
Gary Warriner, Conway Arena General Manager 
Candace Sullivan, Conway Arena Customer Service Manager 
 
Approval of Previous Meeting’s Minutes 
Motion made to approve the previous meeting’s minutes (7/28/25) by Charlie Hall. Seconded by Lori 
Wilshire. 
Motion passed unanimously.
3 
 
Updates 
General Manager Gary Warriner provided an update of operations of the area: 
• General rate for ice time is $300/hour, about $50 lower than market rate.  
• The arena has kept the public skate rate the same at $5 for two hours, which has not changed 
since 2003. 
• Given the age of the building, maintenance and repairs are ongoing. 
• The settlement issue in the corner of the building has been fully repaired. This was the arena’s 
largest expense of approximately $180,000, which came from their reserves. 
• In the next year, the arena will replace all four entry doors in the front of the building. The 
current doors are not handicap accessible. The new doors will have push button access. The 
upgrade will cost between $50,000-$60,000 when completed. 
• Conway Arena has awarded over $1,000,000 in grants since its inception. Due to the cost of 
the settlement repair, Conway will be awarding $45,000 this year, which is lower than usual. 
 
Budget 
General Manager Gary Warriner presented the 2026-2027 operating budget: 
• Gross revenue: $1.28M 
• Gross expenses: $1.25M 
• Gross profit: $30,000 after $60,000 in reserves. 
• The last major revenue boost was Rivier coming in four years ago for daytime ice rental. The 
ice time continues to be maxed out.  
• Utilities are increasing ($180,000 budgeted), but the solar panels do help with costs. 
o After utilities, the maintenance and repairs line is the largest expense ($130,000). 
• Conway continues to operate debt-free. 
 
Motion made to approve the annual budget for 2026-2027 by Charlie Hall. Seconded by Megan 
Caron. Motion passed unanimously. 
 
Grant Applications 
• The arena received $156,210 in requests. $45,000 is available to award. 
• The commission reviewed each of the 2026 community grant applications. Applications that 
focused on youth athletics were prioritized. 
o 15 recipients were selected. 
• Award ceremony will be held on July 28th at 1:30 PM.  
 
Motion made to award the selected grant recipients by Charlie Hall. Seconded by Lori Wilshire. 
Motion passed unanimously.
3 
General Discussion 
General Manager Gary Warriner stated that parking enforcement has been an issue for the last 18 
months. There has been a significant increase in ticketing, and city equipment is taking up space in 
the overflow lot. “No Parking” signs went up recently in certain spots where it was previously allowed. 
He asked to meet with the Parking Department. Megan Caron agreed to facilitate a meeting. 
 
Adjournment 
Lori Wilshire motioned to adjourn at 11:31 AM. Seconded by Charlie Hall. Motion passed 
unanimously.

Team Tesseract Robotics respectfully requests $2,500 to support our year-round robotics competition program and free community STEM outreach initiatives serving 
youth throughout Nashua and Southern New Hampshire.
Team Tesseract is a student-led FIRST Tech Challenge robotics team where students design, build, program, test, and compete with custom-built robots. While 
competition is a key component of our program, our mission extends far beyond the playing field. We use robotics as a platform to provide free, hands-on STEM 
learning opportunities, introduce families to FIRST robotics programs, mentor younger students, and inspire the next generation of innovators, engineers, and 
community leaders.
Our program is built around two interconnected goals. First, we provide team members with meaningful experiences in engineering, programming, design, business, 
project management, outreach, and leadership. Students gain real-world skills while working collaboratively to solve complex challenges and prepare for future 
academic and career opportunities.
Second, we leverage the knowledge, resources, and confidence developed through competition to expand access to STEM education in our community. Through 
demonstrations, workshops, mentoring programs, and outreach events, we create engaging and accessible STEM experiences for younger students and their families. 
When children see a student-designed robot move, score, and respond to code, STEM concepts come to life in a way that is exciting, tangible, and inspiring.
Support for Team Tesseract helps sustain both aspects of our mission—allowing students to participate in a high-quality competitive robotics program while also 
expanding free STEM learning opportunities that benefit youth throughout the Greater Nashua region.

Upbeat New Hampshire (Upbeat), based in Nashua, is a nonprofit music education program providing free or low-cost string instrument instruction through ensemble-

The YMCA is exploring implementation of the nationally recognized Teen Mental Health First Aid  program. Teen Mental Health First Aid is an evidence-based 
prevention and education program  designed for youth ages 14-18 that teaches teens how to recognize signs of mental health and  substance use challenges in 
themselves and their peers, how to have supportive conversations,  and how to connect a friend with a trusted adult when additional help is needed. 
The program addresses topics including anxiety, depression, bullying, social media impacts,  substance use, ADHD, eating disorders, and other common adolescent 
mental health concerns. Students learn practical intervention skills and a structured action plan for supporting peers while understanding the importance of involving 
trusted adults. 
Goals 
1. Increase mental health literacy among local teens. 
2. Reduce stigma surrounding mental health challenges. 
3. Equip youth with practical skills to recognize warning signs in peers. 
4. Strengthen connections between youth and trusted adults. 
5. Increase early identification and referral of youth experiencing mental health concerns. 
6. Build a more supportive and inclusive youth community.
